name: MedOdyssey
description: A medical long-context benchmark ranging from 4,000 to 200,000 tokens, incorporating 'needle in a haystack' tasks adapted for medical documentation including patient records, clinical notes, and medical literature. Tests whether LLMs can accurately retrieve and reason over clinically relevant information embedded in long medical documents — a critical capability for real clinical deployment.
typical_sota_score: ~40–65% (frontier models; performance degrades significantly at longer context lengths)
reputation: Published at ACL 2025; addresses critical gap in medical LLM evaluation for long-context clinical scenarios; 200K token contexts reflect real-world clinical document lengths
notes: ACL 2025. Medical long-context evaluation is clinically important because real patient records can span years of documentation. Needle-in-a-haystack tasks adapted to medical domain: retrieving specific lab values, medication orders, or diagnoses from lengthy clinical notes. 4K–200K token range covers short encounter notes to comprehensive longitudinal records. Performance drops more dramatically for medical tasks than general NIAH, suggesting medical terminology and clinical reasoning add difficulty beyond simple retrieval.
